stimuli.text: A block of mass 3 kg on a 20° incline is connected by a light string over a light, frictionless pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging block of mass 3 kg. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is 0.15. The system is released from rest, and the hanging block descends.
A block of mass 1.1 kg on a horizontal frictionless surface is attached to a spring. Its position is $$x(t) = 0.18\cos(11t)$$, with x in meters and t in seconds.
Students measure the period of a simple pendulum for several string lengths, using small amplitudes.
A solid cylinder (I = ½MR²) and a solid sphere (I = ⅖MR²) of equal mass M and radius R are released from rest at the top of the same ramp of height 2 m. Both roll without slipping.

questions.stem: A 6 kg cart moving at 12 m/s collides with and sticks to a 8 kg cart at rest. What is their speed after the collision?

options.why: Kinetic energy is not conserved here.
Correct. Momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is not.
Use m₁v₁ for the initial momentum.

questions.explanation: v_f = 6·12/14 = 5.14 m/s; kinetic energy lost = 247 J.

questions.stem: A 0.7 kg ball hits a wall at 19 m/s and rebounds at 13 m/s. The contact lasts 0.02 s. What is the average force from the wall?

options.why: Correct. Δp = m(v_f − v_i) with the direction reversed.
The velocity reverses, so the speeds add.

questions.stem: An oscillator's position is $$x(t) = 0.12\cos(4t)$$ m. What is its maximum speed?
A car rounds a flat curve of radius 60 m. The coefficient of static friction is 0.9. What is the maximum speed without skidding?

options.why: Correct. Static friction supplies the centripetal force: μmg = mv²/r.

questions.stem: A planet has 2 times Earth's mass and 0.5 times Earth's radius. What is the gravitational field strength at its surface? (Earth's is 9.8 N/kg.)
A spring with $$k = 90$$ N/m is compressed 0.07 m and launches a 0.2 kg block across a frictionless surface. What is the block's speed after leaving the spring?

options.why: The ½ appears on both sides.

questions.stem: A wheel spinning at 16 rad/s slows uniformly to rest in 12 s. How many revolutions does it make while stopping?

options.why: The average angular speed is ω₀/2.
Correct. Δθ = ½ω₀t, then divide by 2π.
That is in radians; convert to revolutions.

questions.stem: Masses of 10 kg and 2 kg hang on either side of a light, frictionless pulley. What is the magnitude of their acceleration?

options.why: The masses are connected, so a is less than g.
The whole system accelerates: divide by both masses.

questions.stem: Two springs with constants 60 N/m and 90 N/m are connected in series and support a 3.5 kg mass at rest. How far do they stretch in total?

options.why: Series and parallel rules are reversed.
The force is the weight, mg.

questions.stem: A simple pendulum is 2.1 m long. What is its period for small oscillations?
A spring with $$k = 340$$ N/m is compressed 0.1 m and launches a 0.5 kg block across a frictionless surface. What is the block's speed after leaving the spring?

options.why: The ½ appears on both sides.

questions.stem: An object of mass 0.1 kg falls from rest with a drag force $$F = -bv$$, where $$b = 0.16$$ kg/s. What is its speed at $$t = m/b$$?

options.why: Correct. v = v_T(1 − e^(−t/τ)) and t = τ.
Terminal speed is reached only as t → ∞.

questions.explanation: v_T = mg/b = 6.13 m/s and τ = m/b = 0.625 s.

questions.stem: A car moving at 9 m/s brakes with a constant deceleration of 6 m/s². How far does it travel before stopping?

options.why: That is the stopping time in seconds.
Correct. Use v² = v₀² + 2aΔx with v = 0.

questions.stem: A boat points straight across a river 70 m wide, moving at 3 m/s relative to the water. The current flows at 1 m/s. How long does the crossing take?

options.why: The current is perpendicular to the heading.
The perpendicular component alone sets the crossing time.
Correct. The current does not change the time to cross; it only carries the boat downstream.
The current is perpendicular to the heading.

questions.stem: A constant torque of 7 N·m acts on a wheel ($$I = 0.8$$ kg·m²) initially at rest, through 7 revolutions. What is the wheel's final angular speed?

options.why: Correct. Work τΔθ (in radians) equals ½Iω².

questions.stem: A 61 kg person stands on a scale in an elevator that is accelerating downward at 4 m/s². What does the scale read?

options.why: Check the direction of the acceleration.
Correct. The scale reads the normal force: N − mg = ma (up positive).
The acceleration changes the normal force.

questions.stem: A ball rolls off a horizontal ledge 5.5 m high at 12 m/s. How far from the base of the ledge does it land?

options.why: Correct. Fall time from the height, times the horizontal speed.
Horizontal and vertical motion are independent.
Take the square root for the time.

questions.stem: A 0.7 kg mass oscillates on a spring with $$k = 65$$ N/m. What is the period?
A motor lifts a 460 kg load 23 m at constant speed in 28 s. What average power does it deliver?

options.why: That is the work; divide by time.

questions.stem: The potential energy of a particle is $$U(x) = 4x^3 - 3x$$ J. At what positive x is the particle in stable equilibrium?

options.why: Set the derivative, not U, to zero.
Correct. Equilibrium where dU/dx = 0; stable at a minimum.

questions.explanation: dU/dx = 12x² − 3 = 0 gives x = 0.5 m; d²U/dx² > 0 there, so it is stable.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of length 1.3 m is pivoted at one end and released from rest in a horizontal position. What is its angular acceleration just after release?

options.why: Correct. τ = Mg(L/2) and I = ML²/3 give α = 3g/(2L).
Use τ = Iα with I = ML²/3.

questions.stem: Satellite B orbits a planet in a circular orbit 4 times the radius of satellite A's circular orbit. What is the ratio of B's orbital speed to A's?
A 4 kg mass hangs from a light string wrapped around a uniform disk pulley of mass 1 kg that turns on a frictionless axle. What is the acceleration of the mass?

options.why: The pulley's inertia reduces the acceleration.
Correct. a = mg/(m + M/2), using I = ½MR² and a = Rα.

questions.explanation: mg − T = ma and TR = ½MR²(a/R) give a = 8.71 m/s².

questions.stem: A uniform 4 m beam weighing 100 N rests on supports at both ends. A 600 N load sits 3 m from the left end. What force does the right support exert?

options.why: Correct. Take torques about the left support.
The load is not at the center.
Include the beam's weight at its center.
That is the left support's force.

questions.stem: A uniform disk of mass 3 kg and radius 0.2 m spins at 19 rad/s on a frictionless axle. A 1.25 kg lump of clay is dropped onto the rim and sticks. What is the new angular speed?

options.why: Correct. Angular momentum is conserved: I_iω_i = I_fω_f.
Kinetic energy is not conserved in a sticking collision.

questions.stem: A block starts from rest and slides 10 m down a 30° incline with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.2. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
Correct. mgh − μmg cos θ·L = ½mv².
Use the vertical drop, L sin θ.

questions.explanation: h = 5 m. v = √(2g(h − μL cos θ)) = 8 m/s.

questions.stem: A force $$F(x) = 5x^2$$ N acts along the x-axis. How much work does it do on an object moving from $$x = 2$$ m to $$x = 5$$ m?

options.why: Integrate; do not just evaluate F.

questions.stem: An object's acceleration is $$a(t) = 6t$$ m/s². At $$t = 0$$ it has velocity 3 m/s and is at $$x = 0$$. What is its position at $$t = 3$$ s?

options.why: Correct. Integrate twice, using the initial conditions.

questions.stem: A 5 kg object at rest experiences a net force $$F(t) = 7t$$ N from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 3$$ s. What is its final speed?

options.why: Correct. Impulse ∫F dt equals the change in momentum.
Divide by the mass to get speed.

questions.stem: A 3 kg ball moving at +2 m/s collides elastically head-on with a 4 kg ball at rest. What is the velocity of the 4 kg ball afterward (positive in the original direction)?

options.why: That would be a sticking collision.
Correct. Elastic: conserve momentum and kinetic energy (relative velocity reverses).

questions.explanation: v₁' = (m₁ − m₂)v/(m₁ + m₂) = -0.286 m/s; v₂' = 2m₁v/(m₁ + m₂) = 1.71 m/s.

questions.stem: A mass on a spring oscillates with angular frequency 10 rad/s and amplitude 0.1 m. What is its speed when it is 0.04 m from equilibrium?

options.why: Use A² − x² under a square root.
Speed is greatest at equilibrium, not at the ends.
That is the maximum speed, at x = 0.
Correct. v = ω√(A² − x²), from conservation of energy.

questions.stem: A 1000 kg car heading east at 15 m/s collides with a 500 kg car heading north at 20 m/s, and they lock together. What is their speed just after the collision?

options.why: Momentum is a vector; add components at right angles.
Weight each velocity by its mass.
Correct. Conserve momentum in x and y separately, then combine.

questions.stem: A ball is launched from level ground at 18 m/s at 30° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance, what is its maximum height?

options.why: Use the vertical component, v₀ sin θ.
Correct. Treat horizontal and vertical motion separately.

questions.explanation: v₀x = 15.6 m/s, v₀y = 9 m/s. H = v₀y²/(2g) = 4.13 m.

questions.stem: A 4 kg block on a horizontal table is connected by a string over a light pulley to a hanging 1 kg block. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the table and the block is 0.1. What is the acceleration of the blocks?

options.why: Include friction on the table block.
Correct. Net force (m₂g − μm₁g) divided by the total mass.
Both blocks accelerate; divide by the total mass.

questions.stem: A constant torque of 11 N·m acts on a wheel ($$I = 1.3$$ kg·m²) initially at rest, through 4 revolutions. What is the wheel's final angular speed?

options.why: Correct. Work τΔθ (in radians) equals ½Iω².

questions.stem: What is the rotational inertia of a uniform rod of mass 5 kg and length 1 m about an axis through one end, perpendicular to the rod?

options.why: The mass is spread along the rod.
Correct. I = ML²/3 (parallel-axis theorem from ML²/12).

questions.stem: A rod lies along the x-axis from $$x = 0$$ to $$x = 4$$ m and has linear mass density $$\lambda = kx^3$$. Where is its center of mass?

options.why: The exponents are n + 2 and n + 1.

questions.stem: A planet has mass $$6 \times 10^{25}$$ kg and radius $$4 \times 10^{6}$$ m. What is the escape speed from its surface? ($$G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}$$ N·m²/kg²)

options.why: That is the circular orbit speed; escape needs √2 times more.

questions.stem: A 2 kg ball on a 0.7 m string moves in a vertical circle. At the top of the circle its speed is 5 m/s. What is the tension in the string there?

options.why: Check the direction of gravity relative to the center.
Correct. At the top, T + mg = mv²/r.

questions.stem: A 18 g bullet moving at 290 m/s embeds in a 4.6 kg block hanging from strings. How high does the block rise?

options.why: Correct. Momentum for the collision, then energy for the swing.
Kinetic energy is not conserved in the collision.
Find the block's speed after the collision first.

questions.explanation: V = 1.13 m/s after the collision; h = V²/(2g) = 0.0652 m.

questions.title: Block on an incline with a hanging mass

parts.prompt: Draw (describe) a free-body diagram for the 3 kg block, labeling each force.

rubric.criterion: Weight down, normal force perpendicular to the incline, tension up the incline.
Kinetic friction down the incline (opposite the motion).

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the acceleration of the system in terms of the masses, θ, μ and g, then calculate its value.

rubric.criterion: Newton's second law applied to each block (or the system).

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the string.
Calculate the speed of the blocks after the hanging block has descended 2 m, and the work done by friction on the incline block during that motion.

rubric.criterion: Work by friction, with a negative sign.

parts.prompt: Sketch (describe) graphs of position, velocity and acceleration versus time for one period, aligned vertically.

rubric.criterion: Position is a cosine starting at +A; velocity is a negative sine starting at 0.
rubric.example: x starts at 0.18 m; v starts at 0 and goes negative.

rubric.criterion: Acceleration starts at its negative maximum and is opposite in sign to position throughout.

parts.prompt: Derive expressions for v(t) and a(t), and determine the maximum speed and maximum acceleration.
Calculate the spring constant and the period.
Calculate the total mechanical energy and describe how kinetic and potential energy vary during one period.

rubric.example: K is maximum at x = 0 and zero at x = ±A; U is the reverse; the sum is constant. Each varies twice per period.

parts.prompt: Describe a procedure the students could use to measure the period accurately, including how to reduce uncertainty.

rubric.example: Time 10 swings with a stopwatch and divide by 10.

rubric.criterion: Keep the amplitude small and repeat trials.
rubric.example: Release from under about 10° and average several trials.

parts.prompt: Identify quantities to graph that would give a straight line, and explain how g can be found from the graph.
Plot (describe) the linearized data and draw a best-fit line. Use it to calculate an experimental value of g.
The students repeat the experiment with a much larger amplitude. Predict how the measured periods would change and explain.

rubric.criterion: Periods increase slightly; the small-angle approximation (sin θ ≈ θ) no longer holds.
rubric.example: The restoring torque is less than proportional to θ at large angles.

parts.prompt: Without calculating, predict which object reaches the bottom first. Justify your prediction using energy.

rubric.example: It has the smaller rotational inertia per MR².

rubric.criterion: Justification: less of its energy goes into rotation, so more is translational kinetic energy.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the speed at the bottom of an object with rotational inertia βMR², in terms of g, h and β.

rubric.criterion: Energy conservation including both forms of kinetic energy, with v = Rω.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of each object at the bottom.

rubric.example: solid cylinder: 5.11 m/s; solid sphere: 5.29 m/s

parts.prompt: Explain whether your derived expression is consistent with your prediction in part (a), and why neither speed depends on M or R.

rubric.criterion: Smaller β gives larger v, consistent with the prediction.
M and R cancel in the energy equation.
rubric.example: Only the shape factor β matters.
